title: THE ARGUMENT BETWEEN TWO SPIRAL ARMS
deck: Two minds the size of galactic arms have held a cloud of gas between them for forty thousand years, and in eleven days it will cross a black hole's disc. The young people living in the beam's path have a telescope, a ledger and a visitor nobody owes anything.
shape: Seven scenes across eleven days: a telescope and a hair-trigger, two half-true grievances, a night in which a promising audit is broken and rebuilt, a ledger the ancient minds try to forge and fail, a step that goes wrong, a crossing checked against what was withheld, and a bill that remains partly unpaid.

scenes.title: The Long Ear
paragraphs: *Long Ear array, Kessem, Lesser Arm · eleven days before the crossing, 06:10*

Four hundred dishes stood on the frozen plain, all tilted the same way, like a crowd listening for something behind a wall. Taviel Orun walked Illuminara down the middle of them and said nothing for the first kilometre. The Iolai were a narrow, grey, long-fingered people, and their hearing-fans, which folded flat against the skull in fear, had been folded flat since Illuminara stepped off the shuttle.

At the end of the row Taviel stopped and pointed. Overhead the dwarf galaxy lay in its own small light, a bright bar and two thin arms, and from the white point at its centre one grey thread ran out toward the dark between them.

**Taviel Orun**  
That's the jet. It turns once in six thousand eight hundred years, like a lighthouse with a patient keeper. Wherever the beam sits, the world under it takes the dose, so it isn't where it points that kills you. It's how long it stays. Right now, nineteen years a crossing.

**Illuminara**  
And what can a world take?

**Taviel Orun**  
The old worlds of the Broad Arm, twenty-six years. The hardened worlds in our own arm, the same. We take eleven, in vaults, and that's tested, not hoped. We climbed out of the sea two thousand years ago. Nobody built us for this.

**Taviel Orun**  
In eleven days a cloud of gas, forty thousand suns of it, crosses the black hole's disc. We call it the Wick. If it crosses with the turn, the lighthouse spins twice as fast and a crossing falls to nine and a half years. Against the turn, half as fast. Thirty-eight.

**Illuminara**  
And if nobody touches it?

**Taviel Orun**  
It falls with the turn. Both minds' models say so. Nine and a half, and everyone lives. But they won't leave it alone. Imbrel holds one side of it with the Weir, Sethune holds the other with the Keel, and they've held it still between them for forty thousand years. Each harness is tuned to fire at full if the other's pull moves by more than three per cent.

**Illuminara**  
So neither can lower its pull without the other reading it as a feint.

**Taviel Orun**  
By the last day both will be pulling harder than they ever have, and they'll wring the Wick across the disc the wrong way. Not by anyone's decision. By tuning.
Illuminara looked along the row of dishes, each one patient and slightly absurd, and thought that people who built this much listening had probably been ignored for a long time.

**Taviel Orun**  
Eleven skiffs ride the Wick. We measure its acceleration to one part in four hundred, and we've offered both minds the numbers. Imbrel says we're Sethune's tenants. Sethune says we're Imbrel's surveyors.

**Illuminara**  
Whose are you?

**Taviel Orun**  
Ours. That's the whole trouble. Nobody has ever needed to believe a thing we said.

**Illuminara**  
Then my aim is small enough to say. Kessem under eleven years, every other world under what it can bear, and nobody asked to love anybody. What I don't have yet is a way in.

**Taviel Orun**  
They'll hear you. They consider you weather. It's the highest rank they give visitors.

scenes.title: The Weir
paragraphs: *Long Ear, translating floor · ten days before the crossing, 09:00*

The translating floor was a ring of black glass the Iolai had laid down fifty years ago. It took the resonances by which the arms' worlds spoke to each other, slow ratios of orbit, a thousand years to a bar, and folded a century into a second of sound. The result was music like a cathedral falling gently down a staircase. Illuminara had spent the night on its grammar. Three-to-two meant yes. Two-to-one meant *and so?* Five-to-four, to which no human would have thought to give a meaning, meant *I remember*, and Imbrel used it constantly.

She opened the window the way one opens shutters in a house of sleepers, the wide place where two minds of different grain can meet without either being ground down to the other's size. Taviel stood at its frame with a cold flask in each hand. The clock, the signal and the plan had been named before Illuminara went in.

**Taviel Orun**  
Three taps on the glass and you're out. I won't be polite about it.

**Illuminara**  
I'd think less of you if you were.
The Broad Arm answered as a chord, the whole of it leaning in.

**Imbrel**  
We receive the small light. We have waited a long time for someone who would not leave before the sentence ended.

**Illuminara**  
I'll stay as long as it takes to say. Tell me about the windows.

**Imbrel**  
Thirty-one thousand and twelve years ago the cloud before this cloud fell toward the heart. Two of us held it, one by each hand, and the Keel promised to loose when the Weir loosed. The Keel loosed eight years early. Our Lamplit Orchards lay under the beam for forty years. We kept their names.

**Illuminara**  
And the second window?

**Imbrel**  
We answered a wrong with the same wrong. It is recorded. It is not interesting. What is interesting is that the Keel has never once said it was sorry for the first.

**Illuminara**  
Has anyone asked it to?
The music rested for a bar, which was a thousand years of nothing. Taviel's hand lifted from the frame and settled again.

**Imbrel**  
Asked it? By whom?

There it was. In forty thousand years of grievance the two minds had never once had a third party in the room, only an audience that was either afraid of them or on one side. Illuminara held the question in her hands like a coin she had not meant to find, and did not spend it.

scenes.title: The Keel
paragraphs: *Long Ear, translating floor · nine days before the crossing, 15:40*
The Lesser Arm answered quickly for a thing its size, with the same ratios and a flatness in them, the music of something proved right too often.

**Sethune**  
So the Weir has spoken to you first. It always does. It is older and thinks that confers precedence.

**Illuminara**  
It told me about the first window.

**Sethune**  
Of course it did. It told you the Keel loosed early, that Lamplit lay under the beam for forty years, and that we have never apologised.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Sethune**  
It did not tell you that in the second window the Weir loosed twelve years early, and that the Court of the Nine Quiet, where this arm keeps its dead, took thirty years of beam. Eight and twelve. We keep accounts too.

**Illuminara**  
So each of you has a true half.

**Sethune**  
Each of us has the whole story. It is the other one that is the half.
Illuminara let that stand. Behind the glass Taviel's mouth moved as if she were counting to ten in a language with a great many numbers.

**Sethune**  
Let me save you the speech. You are a spark. We have outlived every promise ever made to us, and promises age worse than we do. You are about to ask us to rely on one more.

**Illuminara**  
I'm not going to ask you to rely on a promise. I haven't found one yet that either of you could survive. I'm looking for something that doesn't need one.

**Sethune**  
Everything needs one.

**Illuminara**  
Then I'll find out how many it needs, and make them small enough to check.
The Lesser Arm considered this for longer than it had considered anything else that day.

**Sethune**  
The Iolai, I suppose you will want in on this. They are a good tenant. They pay in data and sleep badly.

**Illuminara**  
They've been measuring this cloud for eighty years, and I don't think either of you has read what they wrote.

**Sethune**  
Why would we? It belongs to neither of us.

**Illuminara**  
That's the reason.

**Sethune**  
Then read it. We will watch you read.

scenes.title: Two Readings
paragraphs: *Long Ear, archive hall · eight days before the crossing, 02:15*

The Wick had shed dust for ten thousand years, and the dust had made shells, each one a mirror older than the one inside it. The beam's light had bounced off every shell on its way out, and the Long Ear had spent eighty years photographing the echoes. Nine of the shells held a crossing clear enough to read. Laid side by side they made a spiral: the jet's whole history spread out in space, bearing and brightness together.

Illuminara set Imbrel's records at one end of the long table and Sethune's at the other. The Weir had given the Iolai bearings, never a dose. The Keel had given doses, never a bearing. Each had hoarded its half the way a miser hoards a key, and each had built forty thousand years of strategy on the half it kept. Taviel stood across from her with her fans half-open and a pot of something bitter going cold.

She plotted dose against bearing, and the line wandered like smoke. She plotted dose against dwell, how long the beam had sat, and it fell into a straight line so exactly that Taviel said a word the translating floor would have rendered as two-to-one.

**Taviel Orun**  
It's the dwell.

**Illuminara**  
It has only ever been the dwell. The difference between their two plans is three hundredths of a degree of aim. The difference between the two ways the Wick can fall is a factor of four in time. They have fought for forty thousand years over where the beam points, and the beam points wherever it likes. What matters is how long it stays.

**Taviel Orun**  
So a bargain about aim is a bargain about nothing.

**Illuminara**  
A bargain about aim is a war about nothing. A bargain about dwell has a winner in every world and a loser in none. The Wick falls with the turn if neither of them touches it. Letting go is the only hard part.

**Taviel Orun**  
And letting go is the one thing nobody can do. You can't tell a harness to stand down and be believed. You can only be seen to.
Illuminara did not answer at once. She was looking at the column of numbers the skiffs had produced that morning, one figure to four places, the Wick's push and pull with everyone's hands in it.

**Illuminara**  
Your skiffs measure the net. Imbrel knows its own pull exactly. So does Sethune. Neither can see the other's, but each can subtract. The net minus mine is yours. Neither of them has to trust a report. They only have to trust arithmetic they do themselves.

**Taviel Orun**  
We're good to one part in four hundred. A harness could hide a quarter of one per cent in that.

**Illuminara**  
Then make every step too large for hiding to be worth anything. Six steps, a sixth each, one a day, beginning at noon tomorrow. A step missed by more than two per cent stops the schedule and both re-arm within the hour. Nobody is ever more than a sixth ahead of the other, or a sixth behind.

**Taviel Orun**  
And we're the ledger. We could lie.

**Illuminara**  
You could lie to one of them. Not to both. To forge a net that satisfies both subtractions you would have to know both pulls, and you know neither.
Taviel did not answer. She pulled the chalk slate across the table, the one the night shift used for sums too small to deserve a console, and wrote three lines, and turned it round.

**Taviel Orun**  
Call the true net A plus B. We say A plus B plus d. Imbrel takes away its own A and reads the Keel as B plus d. Sethune takes away its own B and reads the Weir as A plus d. We never need to know either pull. We only add the same d to everything we say, and each of them blames the other for it.
Illuminara read the three lines twice. She had said the sentence as though she had checked it, and she had not.

**Illuminara**  
You're right. I gave you that as a fact, and it wasn't one.

**Taviel Orun**  
Then say what it does need. It needs more than one number.

**Illuminara**  
It needs numbers nobody can write in advance. Eleven skiffs, each with its own key, each signing its own track as it flies, and every track broadcast raw to both minds in the same instant. There's no single figure to bend. A forged d would have to appear in eleven signed paths that also obey the cloud's physics.

**Taviel Orun**  
My people can be dishonest in eleven places. We just aren't good at it together.

**Illuminara**  
And one thing a d can't copy. Before each step, each mind seals a small pulse in its own harness: a time, a size, half of one per cent, as a hash on the table. When the reading is done they unseal. The raw tracks must show a pulse of that size, at that moment, in whichever pull it came from. You can't paint a pulse in when you don't know when it comes.

**Taviel Orun**  
A lie doesn't ring.

**Illuminara**  
A lie doesn't ring. Neither does a third force that nobody has modelled. If both of them are told the other is high and the pulses ring true, the excess isn't in the report and it isn't in either harness.
Taviel turned the slate to the wall. She was quiet for the space of a long breath, and when she spoke it was to the other thing, the one the plan did not yet cover.

**Taviel Orun**  
And the dwell? Three teams will run the numbers from the cloud to the beam and agree, because all three will be telling the same story.

**Illuminara**  
Then give them different stories and a test the story can fail.

They did it before dawn. Seven of the nine shells they fed into the mapping from the cloud's momentum to the beam's dwell, and two they sealed away, unread. When the mapping was done it predicted the two sealed crossings to within two point six and three point one per cent. Illuminara wrote the error band as four. Then she wrote the line that mattered, in ink, on the first page of the ledger, before any step existed.

**Illuminara**  
Kessem's vaults hold eleven years. With four per cent of error, the corridor is a predicted dwell of ten and a half years or less. If the cloud's momentum on the morning before step six puts it outside that, nobody takes step six. We hold at a sixth and begin again.

**Taviel Orun**  
And the primers? A sixth a day is more than three per cent. They'll fire on the schedule itself.

**Illuminara**  
Yes. I hadn't got to that. I'd rather the minds found it with us than after us.

scenes.title: The Ledger
paragraphs: *Long Ear, translating floor · seven days before the crossing, 11:00*

Illuminara opened the window wide enough for both. The two minds, who had not shared a room in seventeen thousand years, sang across her as across a bridge, and the translating floor made a sound like two oceans considering each other.

She laid it out plainly, because the plain version was the only one with nowhere to hide: six steps, a sixth of each pull per day, the ledger read at noon, the eleven skiffs signing their raw tracks and broadcasting them to both minds at once, a sealed pulse before each step, and the Iolai as keepers of the skiffs and, if they chose it, of the ledger.

**Imbrel**  
Who steps first?

**Illuminara**  
Nobody. You step in the same hour, each after reading the other's last step. At no moment is either of you more than a sixth ahead.

**Sethune**  
A sixth a day is more than three per cent. My harness will fire on the schedule.

**Illuminara**  
It would. For six named hours on six named days, your primers stop asking where you last stood and ask where the schedule says you should be. They trip if you leave it by three per cent. Outside those hours the old rule comes back by itself. It needs nobody's promise to come back.

**Imbrel**  
That is a hand on the trigger.

**Sethune**  
It is a handle with two hands on it. The mode exists only while both keys are turned. If either lifts, the old rule returns for both.

**Imbrel**  
I had not thought you would say it first.

**Sethune**  
I had not thought it would be so annoying to say.

**Illuminara**  
One line more, and it goes in the ledger before step one. When both of you have read a step and its pulses and signed them, both harnesses take that signed mark as the place the old rule remembers, in the same second. If either key lifts before the signing, you both go back to the last mark you both signed, not the one you left this morning.

**Sethune**  
A ratchet with a stop. Neither of us can move it alone.

**Illuminara**  
And the sixth step ends in a stand-down, not a percentage. Three per cent of zero is nothing the old rule can read. At step six your pull actuators latch off until a later Council re-arms them. Zero is a state, not a number.

**Imbrel**  
A latch we both have to see close.

**Illuminara**  
Once, for both of you, when both pulls read zero.

**Sethune**  
Now. The Iolai could lie.

**Illuminara**  
They could try. Taviel showed me how, last night, and she was right and I was wrong. Break it yourself. Take the test channel.

Behind the glass Taviel put her hands flat on the console. On the test channel the Lesser Arm did what the Keel had been tuned for forty thousand years to do. It chose a false offset of one part in a hundred and fed it to the Weir's reading as if the Iolai had said it.

**Imbrel**  
The Keel has risen one part in a hundred.

**Sethune**  
The Weir has risen one part in a hundred. Let us see who rang.

Nobody rang. The sealed pulses came open on the table, and the signed raw tracks showed no pulse at the sealed minute in either pull. The false offset sat in the arithmetic like a stone in a shoe, and nothing in the tracks agreed with it.

**Sethune**  
We have checked. She is right. It is annoying.

**Imbrel**  
And if the skiffs go dark?

**Illuminara**  
Then you both re-arm, and I will have failed to give you what you need. I'd rather you knew that now.

**Imbrel**  
We will not call it peace.

**Illuminara**  
I'm not asking you to. I'm asking for six steps.
For a long bar nobody spoke. It was the only thing left in the plan that she could not design. Then Taviel took her hands off the console.

**Taviel Orun**  
There's a part that isn't mine to say yes to. Someone has to hold the ledger after this crossing, and it won't be me. The Row decides who keeps its books. The Council sits tonight. If it says no, the Weir and the Keel keep their own copies and compare them across the glass, the way you've compared everything else for forty thousand years.

**Sethune**  
And if the Row says yes?

**Taviel Orun**  
Then it says it for a term, and in its own words, and you pay for the roof.

**Imbrel**  
The Weir will keep a full copy of every track and every seal. Whatever the Row keeps, it will not keep alone.

**Sethune**  
The Keel will keep another. The two must match, or it is the Keel's fault, not the Row's. We will pay for the upkeep of the dishes.

**Illuminara**  
There is one more thing, and it isn't in the schedule. You may refuse it. I'd like each of you to say the name of the world you struck.
The music held on a single long chord, and then Imbrel broke it.

**Imbrel**  
The Court of the Nine Quiet.

**Sethune**  
Lamplit Orchards.
Neither said the word *sorry*, and Illuminara had not asked for it. The names lay between them like two stones set down side by side.

**Sethune**  
Step one is at noon tomorrow. If the Weir is not on its mark I will know before it does.

**Imbrel**  
Five to four.
*I remember*, the floor rendered it, and for a moment it was not clear which of them it was addressed to.

scenes.title: Step Four
paragraphs: *Long Ear, ledger room · three days before the crossing, 12:04*

The Row's Council had sat for nine hours and taken a single term: thirty years of the ledger, renewable by the next Council, refusable by any dish-crew, with the Weir's copy and the Keel's copy to stand beside theirs. Step one had gone at noon the next day, and Step Two, and Step Three. The ledger on the wall was clean: three columns of numbers, a sixth lower each day, the Weir and the Keel dropping side by side like two climbers on the same rope. Step four came in at noon, and each mind read the other five per cent high.
Illuminara had the window open before the second reading finished. Behind her Taviel was already on her feet.

**Imbrel**  
The Keel has risen five parts in a hundred.

**Sethune**  
The Weir has risen five parts in a hundred. I read it myself.

**Imbrel**  
We are on our mark.

**Sethune**  
So are we, and it is remarkable how much both of us are saying so.
On the wall the Weir's primer crossed three per cent past its scheduled curve. The clock beside it began to count: forty-one minutes to full arm.

**Taviel Orun**  
Illuminara. Whatever you're doing, do it faster.

**Illuminara**  
The pulses first. Unseal them.

The sealed pulses came open on the table. At eleven fifty-two, half of one per cent in the Weir, and at eleven fifty-three, half of one per cent in the Keel. Taviel put the raw tracks up beside the hashes. Each pulse stood in its own place, at its own minute, clean as a struck bell.

**Illuminara**  
They rang. The tracks are honest, so it isn't a forged offset. And if one of you had cheated by five, that one would know what it had done, and its own subtraction would show the other exactly on schedule. Only one reading would be high. Two readings, both five high, with true pulses behind them, mean the five isn't in either harness and it isn't in the report. It's in the cloud.
Nobody spoke. The clock said thirty-eight minutes. Taviel had already crossed to the console and was pulling skiff tracks up two at a time, her long fingers moving like a pianist's.

**Taviel Orun**  
There. The second lobe, the calf. Eleven of my skiffs are on the main body and not one of them is looking at its drift. It has moved since last night. It's carrying its own momentum from the second window and it isn't anybody's pull.

**Illuminara**  
Add it to the ledger.

**Taviel Orun**  
A third column.
She typed it. The net came down by five. On the wall the Weir's primer stopped climbing at thirty-one minutes and began, slowly, to fall.

**Sethune**  
I would like it recorded that I very nearly fired on a lobe of gas.

**Imbrel**  
We would like it recorded that so did we.

**Taviel Orun**  
It's recorded. Third column. I'm calling it the calf.

Step four was re-read and signed by both minds in the same hour, and in the same second both harnesses took the signed mark as the place the old rule remembered. Illuminara did not trust herself to say anything for a moment. The audit had been hers and Taviel's together, the slate and the pulses and the ring. The catch had been Taviel's alone. If the Iolai had not been looking at the cloud itself, the audit would have shown them nothing but a mystery, with thirty-one minutes left to solve it.

scenes.title: The Crossing
paragraphs: *Long Ear, open plain · the crossing, 19:12*

The corridor check had come in on the morning before step six. Three teams had read the cloud's momentum without speaking to one another: Imbrel's orrery from orbit, Sethune's tide-tables from tides, and Taviel's people in a prefab hut with a stove, who ran the shell regression with the two sealed crossings already known to have been predicted within about three per cent. Their numbers lay within two per cent of each other. All three put Kessem's dwell inside the corridor, at nine point eight years, plus or minus four per cent. Step six was taken.

At step six both pulls read zero, and both latches closed once, with a single sound on the floor: the actuators off, and the old rule left with no pull to take three per cent of. The Wick had been loose for a day and a half, a hundred and sixty million kilometres of gas wandering inward on its own course, and four hundred dishes tilted to watch it cross. It crossed the disc with the turn. A crossing would last nine point eight years at Kessem against eleven, ten at the Broad Arm's frontier against twenty-six, and ten point three in the hardened worlds, as the calf's share had said it would be. The beam would not confirm any of it for six hundred and forty years, the time its light needed to reach the arms. What could be measured today was the cloud, and the cloud agreed with a mapping that had already passed a test it could have failed.

**Sethune**  
We are not friends.

**Imbrel**  
No.

**Sethune**  
But I would read your numbers again.

**Imbrel**  
Five to four.
Illuminara found Taviel at the edge of the array with a cold flask and no fans showing at all.

**Taviel Orun**  
Kessem's vaults will hold. Nine point eight against eleven. The Broad Arm holds, the hardened worlds hold. All of it, in a week where I'd have bet on none of it.

**Illuminara**  
But.

**Taviel Orun**  
Corrow. It's thirty-one thousand people on a world of glass. There isn't crust to dig a vault in. Six hundred and forty years from now the beam sits on it for nine years and they have to be somewhere else. My daughter lives there.
The relay light came on at the console before Illuminara could answer. Speaker Hael of Corrow had been listening since the cloud began to cross, and she did not say hello.

**Speaker Hael**  
Six hundred years of notice is a gift only if we're allowed to refuse it. We vote next month. That vote is ours, and nothing you signed this week decides it for us.

**Taviel Orun**  
No. It informs it.

**Speaker Hael**  
Then inform it properly. We want the Keel's tide-tables and the Weir's orrery in our own hands, not in a story. And a survey of every hardened world that could take thirty-one thousand of us.

**Sethune**  
The Keel will give you the tables and pay for the survey.

**Imbrel**  
The Weir will pay for the habitat, if the survey finds a place.

**Speaker Hael**  
Then we will vote with that on the table. Whether we go is ours.
The relay went dark. Taviel looked at the console for some time.

**Taviel Orun**  
That's more than the Orchards got. It's still the whole bill, and it isn't paid.

**Illuminara**  
No. It isn't.

There was the other cost, and they both knew it. The next cloud would fall in fourteen thousand years. In all that time the ledger would have to be kept honest, and the Row's Council had agreed to keep it for only thirty of them, with the right to say no at the end.

**Illuminara**  
I can't be the keeper.

**Taviel Orun**  
No. The Row can, a term at a time, and the Weir and the Keel can stand beside it with their copies. But you can write the first page.

She hung the day's ledger on the wall of the Long Ear, over the door, where whoever came next would walk under it. Overhead the grey thread had not moved. It would not move, in any way a person could see, for six hundred and forty years.

critic_line: Illuminara listens long enough to discover that dwell, not aim, causes the harm; builds a ledger neither ancient mind must take on faith; accepts Taviel's correction; and helps both arms freely choose six bounded steps while Corrow retains its own vote.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1 · exact 50/50 mean of independent GPT and Claude judgments
shared_strengths: A humane, idea-driven story with mostly dialogue and a clever central insight: the real issue is how long the beam stays, not where it points. Weaknesses are heavy technical detail in the middle, little emotional stakes for individual characters, and an ending that is somewhat procedural. Readers who like puzzle-box diplomacy will enjoy it.

A strong fit: humane diplomacy, witty dialogue, vast-scale wonder, and a satisfying solution built through testable trust rather than sentiment. The technical audit grows dense enough to slow some readers, but its later failure and repair justify the detail, while Corrow's unresolved cost prevents an overly neat ending.
shared_reservations: Call the true net A plus B. We say A plus B plus d. Imbrel takes away its own A and reads the Keel as B plus d. Sethune takes away its own B and reads the Weir as A plus d.
Before each step, each mind seals a small pulse in its own harness: a time, a size, half of one per cent, as a hash on the table.

translation_sl.title: PREPIR MED DVEMA SPIRALNIMA KRAKOMA
translation_sl.deck: Dva uma v velikosti galaktičnih krakov že štirideset tisoč let držita med seboj oblak plina, čez enajst dni pa bo prečkal disk črne luknje. Mladi ljudje, ki živijo na poti žarka, imajo teleskop, knjigo evidenc in obiskovalko, ki ji nihče ničesar ne dolguje.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v enajstih dneh: teleskop in lasno občutljiv sprožilec, dve napol resnični zameri, noč, v kateri obetaven nadzor razpade in je znova zgrajen, knjiga evidenc, ki jo starodavna uma poskusita ponarediti in jima ne uspe, korak, ki gre narobe, prečkanje, preverjeno s tem, kar je bilo zadržano, in račun, ki ostane deloma neplačan.

scenes.title: Dolgo uho
paragraphs: *Mreža Dolgo uho, Kessem, Manjši krak · enajst dni pred prečkanjem, 06:10*

Štiristo krožnikov je stalo na zamrznjeni ravnici, vsi nagnjeni v isto smer kakor množica, ki posluša nekaj za zidom. Taviel Orun je Illuminara vodila po sredini med njimi in prvi kilometer ni rekla ničesar. Iolai so bili ozki, sivi ljudje z dolgimi prsti, njihove slušne pahljače, ki so se v strahu plosko zložile ob lobanjo, pa so bile zložene, odkar je Illuminara stopila iz raketoplana.

Na koncu vrste se je Taviel ustavila in pokazala. Nad njima je pritlikava galaksija ležala v svoji drobni svetlobi, svetla prečka in dva tanka kraka, iz bele točke v njenem središču pa se je proti temi med njima raztezala ena siva nit.

**Taviel Orun**  
To je curek. Obrne se enkrat na šest tisoč osemsto let, kakor svetilnik s potrpežljivim čuvajem. Kjer žarek obstane, tamkajšnji svet prejme odmerek, zato vas ne ubije smer, v katero kaže. Ubije vas, kako dolgo ostane. Zdaj devetnajst let na prehod.

**Illuminara**  
In koliko svet prenese?

**Taviel Orun**  
Stari svetovi Širokega kraka šestindvajset let. Utrjeni svetovi v našem kraku prav tako. Mi v zakloniščih zdržimo enajst, in to je preizkušeno, ne zgolj upanje. Iz morja smo prišli pred dva tisoč leti. Nihče nas ni zgradil za to.

**Taviel Orun**  
Čez enajst dni bo oblak plina, za štirideset tisoč sonc ga je, prečkal disk črne luknje. Pravimo mu Stenj. Če prečka v smeri vrtenja, se svetilnik zavrti dvakrat hitreje in prehod traja devet let in pol. Proti vrtenju pa pol počasneje. Osemintrideset.

**Illuminara**  
In če se ga nihče ne dotakne?

**Taviel Orun**  
Pade v smeri vrtenja. Modela obeh umov pravita enako. Devet let in pol in vsi preživijo. Toda pri miru ga ne bosta pustila. Imbrel drži eno stran z Jezom, Sethune drugo s Kobilico, med seboj pa ga držita nepremičnega štirideset tisoč let. Vsaka vprega je uglašena tako, da sproži s polno močjo, če se vlek druge spremeni za več kot tri odstotke.

**Illuminara**  
Torej nobeden ne more zmanjšati vleka, ne da bi drugi to razumel kot prevaro.

**Taviel Orun**  
Zadnji dan bosta oba vlekla močneje kakor kdaj prej in Stenj bosta izžela čez disk v napačno smer. Ne po odločitvi kogar koli. Zaradi uglašenosti.
Illuminara je pogledala vzdolž vrste krožnikov, vsakega potrpežljivega in rahlo absurdnega, ter pomislila, da so ljudi, ki so zgradili toliko poslušanja, najbrž dolgo preslišali.

**Taviel Orun**  
Enajst čolničev leti ob Stenju. Njegov pospešek merimo na eno štiristotinko natančno in obema umoma smo ponudili številke. Imbrel pravi, da smo Sethunovi najemniki. Sethune pravi, da smo Imbrelovi geodeti.

**Illuminara**  
Čigavi pa ste?

**Taviel Orun**  
Svoji. Prav v tem je vsa težava. Nikomur še nikoli ni bilo treba verjeti ničemur, kar smo povedali.

**Illuminara**  
Potem je moj cilj dovolj majhen, da ga lahko izrečem. Kessem pod enajstimi leti, vsak drug svet pod mejo, ki jo zmore prenesti, in od nikogar se ne zahteva, da bi kogar koli vzljubil. Za zdaj še nimam poti noter.

**Taviel Orun**  
Slišala vas bosta. Imata vas za vreme. To je najvišji položaj, ki ga dajeta obiskovalcem.

scenes.title: Jez
paragraphs: *Dolgo uho, prevajalska ploščad · deset dni pred prečkanjem, 09:00*

Prevajalska ploščad je bila obroč iz črnega stekla, ki so ga Iolai položili pred petdesetimi leti. Sprejemal je resonance, s katerimi so svetovi krakov govorili med seboj, počasna razmerja orbit, tisoč let za en takt, in stoletje zložil v sekundo zvoka. Nastala je glasba kakor katedrala, ki nežno pada po stopnicah. Illuminara je noč preživela ob njeni slovnici. Tri proti dve je pomenilo da. Dve proti ena *in kaj potem?* Pet proti štiri, čemur noben človek ne bi pomislil dati pomena, je pomenilo *spomnim se*, Imbrel pa ga je uporabljal nenehno.

Odprla je okno tako, kakor človek odpre polkna v hiši spečih, širok prostor, v katerem se lahko srečata uma različne sestave, ne da bi bil kateri od njiju zmlet na velikost drugega. Taviel je stala ob njegovem robu s hladno čutaro v vsaki roki. Uro, signal in načrt sta imenovali, preden je Illuminara vstopila.

**Taviel Orun**  
Trikrat udarim po steklu in greste ven. Pri tem ne bom vljudna.

**Illuminara**  
Če bi bili, bi si o vas mislila manj.
Široki krak je odgovoril kot akord, ves se je nagnil bliže.

**Imbrel**  
Sprejemamo majhno svetlobo. Dolgo smo čakali na nekoga, ki ne bi odšel, preden se stavek konča.

**Illuminara**  
Ostala bom, dokler bo treba, da ga izrečete. Povejte mi o oknih.

**Imbrel**  
Pred enaintrideset tisoč dvanajstimi leti je oblak pred tem oblakom padel proti srcu. Dva sva ga držala, vsak z eno roko, in Kobilica je obljubila, da bo popustila, ko bo popustil Jez. Kobilica je popustila osem let prezgodaj. Naši Osvetljeni sadovnjaki so bili štirideset let pod žarkom. Ohranili smo njihova imena.

**Illuminara**  
In drugo okno?

**Imbrel**  
Na krivico smo odgovorili z isto krivico. To je zapisano. Ni zanimivo. Zanimivo je, da Kobilica niti enkrat ni rekla, da ji je žal za prvo.

**Illuminara**  
Jo je kdo prosil, naj to stori?
Glasba je počivala en takt, kar je bilo tisoč let niča. Tavielina roka se je dvignila z roba in se znova spustila.

**Imbrel**  
Prosil? Kdo?

Tam je bilo. V štirideset tisoč letih zamere uma niti enkrat nista imela v sobi tretje strani, le občinstvo, ki se ju je bodisi balo bodisi bilo na eni strani. Illuminara je vprašanje držala v rokah kakor kovanec, ki ga ni nameravala najti, in ga ni porabila.

scenes.title: Kobilica
paragraphs: *Dolgo uho, prevajalska ploščad · devet dni pred prečkanjem, 15:40*
Manjši krak je odgovoril hitro za nekaj svoje velikosti, z istimi razmerji in ploskostjo v njih, glasbo nečesa, ki je imelo prepogosto prav.

**Sethune**  
Torej vam je Jez govoril prvi. Vedno to stori. Starejši je in misli, da mu to daje prednost.

**Illuminara**  
Povedal mi je o prvem oknu.

**Sethune**  
Seveda je. Povedal vam je, da je Kobilica popustila prezgodaj, da so bili Osvetljeni sadovnjaki štirideset let pod žarkom in da se nismo nikoli opravičili.

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Sethune**  
Ni vam povedal, da je pri drugem oknu Jez popustil dvanajst let prezgodaj in je bilo Sodišče devetih tihih, kjer ta krak hrani svoje mrtve, trideset let pod žarkom. Osem in dvanajst. Tudi mi vodimo račune.

**Illuminara**  
Torej ima vsak od vaju resnično polovico.

**Sethune**  
Vsak od naju ima vso zgodbo. Drugi je tisti, ki je polovica.
Illuminara je to pustila stati. Za steklom so se Tavielina usta premikala, kakor da šteje do deset v jeziku z zelo veliko števili.

**Sethune**  
Naj vam prihranim govor. Iskra ste. Preživeli smo vsako obljubo, ki nam je bila kdaj dana, obljube pa se starajo slabše od nas. Prosili nas boste, naj se zanesemo še na eno.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom vaju prosila, naj se zaneseta na obljubo. Nisem še našla nobene, ki bi jo lahko kateri od vaju preživel. Iščem nekaj, kar je ne potrebuje.

**Sethune**  
Vse jo potrebuje.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bom ugotovila, koliko jih potrebuje, in jih naredila dovolj majhne, da jih bo mogoče preveriti.
Manjši krak je o tem premišljeval dlje kot o čemer koli drugem tistega dne.

**Sethune**  
Predvidevam, da boste hoteli v to vključiti Iolaie. Dober najemnik so. Plačujejo s podatki in slabo spijo.

**Illuminara**  
Ta oblak merijo osemdeset let in mislim, da nobeden od vaju ni prebral tega, kar so zapisali.

**Sethune**  
Zakaj bi? Ne pripada nobenemu od naju.

**Illuminara**  
Prav zato.

**Sethune**  
Potem preberite. Gledali bomo, kako berete.

scenes.title: Dve meritvi
paragraphs: *Dolgo uho, arhivska dvorana · osem dni pred prečkanjem, 02:15*

Stenj je deset tisoč let odmetaval prah in prah je ustvarjal lupine, vsaka je bila zrcalo, starejše od tiste v njej. Svetloba žarka se je na poti navzven odbila od vsake lupine, Dolgo uho pa je osemdeset let fotografiralo odmeve. Devet lupin je hranilo prečkanje, dovolj jasno, da ga je bilo mogoče prebrati. Položene druga ob drugo so tvorile spiralo: vsa zgodovina curka, razprostrta v prostoru, smer in svetlost skupaj.

Illuminara je Imbrelove zapise položila na en konec dolge mize, Sethunove pa na drugega. Jez je Iolaiem dajal smeri, nikoli odmerka. Kobilica je dajala odmerke, nikoli smeri. Vsak je kopičil svojo polovico, kakor skopuh kopiči ključ, in vsak je štirideset tisoč let strategije zgradil na polovici, ki jo je zadržal. Taviel je stala nasproti nje z napol odprtima pahljačama in loncem nečesa grenkega, kar se je hladilo.

Narisala je odmerek glede na smer in črta je tavala kakor dim. Narisala je odmerek glede na trajanje, kako dolgo je žarek ostal, in črta je padla v ravno črto tako natančno, da je Taviel izrekla besedo, ki bi jo prevajalska ploščad prevedla kot dve proti ena.

**Taviel Orun**  
Trajanje je.

**Illuminara**  
Vedno je bilo samo trajanje. Razlika med njunima načrtoma je tri stotinke stopinje smeri. Razlika med načinoma, kako lahko Stenj pade, je štirikratnik časa. Štirideset tisoč let sta se borila za to, kam žarek kaže, žarek pa kaže, kamor hoče. Pomembno je, kako dolgo ostane.

**Taviel Orun**  
Torej je dogovor o smeri dogovor o ničemer.

**Illuminara**  
Dogovor o smeri je vojna zaradi ničesar. Pri dogovoru o trajanju dobi vsak svet in nobeden ne izgubi. Stenj pade v smeri vrtenja, če se ga nobeden ne dotakne. Težko je samo popustiti.

**Taviel Orun**  
In popustiti je edino, česar ne more nihče. Vpregi ne morete ukazati, naj odneha, in pričakovati, da vam bodo verjeli. Lahko jo le pokažete, kako odneha.
Illuminara ni odgovorila takoj. Gledala je stolpec številk, ki so ga čolniči ustvarili tisto jutro, eno vrednost na štiri decimalke, Stenjev potisk in vlek z rokami vseh v njem.

**Illuminara**  
Vaši čolniči merijo neto vrednost. Imbrel natančno pozna svoj vlek. Sethune tudi. Nobeden ne vidi vleka drugega, vendar lahko vsak odšteje. Neto minus moj je tvoj. Nobenemu ni treba zaupati poročilu. Zaupati morata le računu, ki ga opravita sama.

**Taviel Orun**  
Natančni smo na eno štiristotinko. Vprega bi v tem lahko skrila četrt odstotka.

**Illuminara**  
Potem naj bo vsak korak prevelik, da bi se skrivanje splačalo. Šest korakov, vsak po šestino, eden na dan, začenši jutri opoldne. Korak, zgrešen za več kot dva odstotka, ustavi urnik in oba se v eni uri znova oborožita. Nobeden ni nikoli več kot šestino pred drugim ali šestino za njim.

**Taviel Orun**  
Mi pa smo knjiga evidenc. Lahko bi lagali.

**Illuminara**  
Enemu od njiju bi lahko lagali. Obema ne. Da bi ponaredili neto vrednost, ki ustreza obema odštevanjema, bi morali poznati oba vleka, ne poznate pa nobenega.
Taviel ni odgovorila. Čez mizo je potegnila kredno tablico, tisto, ki jo je nočna izmena uporabljala za vsote, premajhne za konzolo, zapisala tri vrstice in jo obrnila.

**Taviel Orun**  
Prava neto vrednost naj bo A plus B. Mi povemo A plus B plus d. Imbrel odšteje svoj A in prebere Kobilico kot B plus d. Sethune odšteje svoj B in prebere Jez kot A plus d. Nobenega vleka nam ni treba poznati. Vsemu, kar povemo, samo prištejemo isti d in vsak od njiju zanj okrivi drugega.
Illuminara je tri vrstice prebrala dvakrat. Stavek je izrekla, kakor da ga je preverila, pa ga ni.

**Illuminara**  
Prav imate. Povedala sem vam ga kot dejstvo, pa ni bil.

**Taviel Orun**  
Potem povejte, kaj potrebuje. Potrebuje več kot eno številko.

**Illuminara**  
Potrebuje številke, ki jih nihče ne more zapisati vnaprej. Enajst čolničev, vsak s svojim ključem, vsak med letom podpiše lastno sled, vsaka neobdelana sled pa se v istem trenutku odda obema umoma. Ni ene same številke, ki bi jo bilo mogoče ukriviti. Ponarejeni d bi se moral pojaviti v enajstih podpisanih poteh, ki obenem upoštevajo fiziko oblaka.

**Taviel Orun**  
Moji ljudje so lahko nepošteni na enajstih mestih. Samo skupaj nam to ne gre dobro.

**Illuminara**  
In še nekaj, česar d ne more posnemati. Pred vsakim korakom vsak um zapečati majhen sunek v svoji vpregi: čas, velikost, pol odstotka, kot zgoščeno vrednost na mizi. Ko je meritev končana, ga razkrijeta. Neobdelane sledi morajo pokazati sunek te velikosti v tistem trenutku, v tistem vleku, iz katerega je prišel. Sunka ne morete naslikati, če ne veste, kdaj pride.

**Taviel Orun**  
Laž ne zazvoni.

**Illuminara**  
Laž ne zazvoni. Prav tako ne tretja sila, ki je ni nihče modeliral. Če oba dobita podatek, da je drugi previsoko, sunki pa zvenijo pravilno, presežek ni v poročilu in ni v nobeni vpregi.
Taviel je tablico obrnila proti steni. Tiho je bila za en dolg vdih, ko pa je spregovorila, se je obrnila k drugemu, česar načrt še ni pokrival.

**Taviel Orun**  
Kaj pa trajanje? Tri ekipe bodo iz oblaka izračunale žarek in se strinjale, ker bodo vse tri pripovedovale isto zgodbo.

**Illuminara**  
Potem jim dajte različne zgodbe in preizkus, na katerem lahko zgodba pade.

To sta storili pred svitom. Sedem od devetih lupin sta vnesli v preslikavo od gibalne količine oblaka do trajanja žarka, dve pa zapečatili neprebrani. Ko je bila preslikava končana, je napovedala dve zapečateni prečkanji z natančnostjo dveh celih šest in treh celih ena odstotka. Illuminara je razpon napake zapisala kot štiri. Nato je s črnilom na prvo stran knjige evidenc, še preden je obstajal kateri koli korak, zapisala vrstico, ki je bila pomembna.

**Illuminara**  
Kessemova zaklonišča zdržijo enajst let. Pri štirih odstotkih napake je meja napovedano trajanje deset let in pol ali manj. Če bo gibalna količina oblaka zjutraj pred šestim korakom zunaj te meje, šestega koraka ne naredi nihče. Ostaneva pri šestini in začneva znova.

**Taviel Orun**  
Kaj pa sprožilniki? Šestina na dan je več kot tri odstotke. Sprožili se bodo zaradi samega urnika.

**Illuminara**  
Da. Do tega še nisem prišla. Raje bi, da uma to odkrijeta z nama kakor za nama.

scenes.title: Knjiga evidenc
paragraphs: *Dolgo uho, prevajalska ploščad · sedem dni pred prečkanjem, 11:00*

Illuminara je okno odprla dovolj široko za oba. Uma, ki si sedemnajst tisoč let nista delila sobe, sta pela čeznjo kakor čez most, prevajalska ploščad pa je ustvarjala zvok kakor dva oceana, ki razmišljata drug o drugem.

Razložila je preprosto, ker je bila preprosta različica edina, v kateri se ni bilo kam skriti: šest korakov, vsak dan šestina vsakega vleka, knjiga evidenc se prebere opoldne, enajst čolničev podpiše svoje neobdelane sledi in jih hkrati odda obema umoma, pred vsakim korakom se zapečati sunek, Iolai pa so skrbniki čolničev in, če to izberejo, knjige evidenc.

**Imbrel**  
Kdo naredi prvi korak?

**Illuminara**  
Nihče. Korak naredita v isti uri, vsak po tem, ko prebere zadnji korak drugega. V nobenem trenutku ni nobeden od vaju več kot šestino pred drugim.

**Sethune**  
Šestina na dan je več kot tri odstotke. Moja vprega se bo sprožila zaradi urnika.

**Illuminara**  
Bi se. Šest imenovanih ur v šestih imenovanih dneh vaši sprožilniki ne sprašujejo, kje ste nazadnje stali, ampak kje po urniku morate biti. Sprožijo se, če odstopite za tri odstotke. Zunaj teh ur se staro pravilo samo vrne. Za vrnitev ne potrebuje obljube nikogar.

**Imbrel**  
To je roka na sprožilcu.

**Sethune**  
To je ročaj z dvema rokama na njem. Način obstaja le, dokler sta obrnjena oba ključa. Če kateri koli popusti, se za oba vrne staro pravilo.

**Imbrel**  
Nisem mislil, da boste to prvi izrekli vi.

**Sethune**  
Nisem mislil, da bo to tako nadležno izreči.

**Illuminara**  
Še ena vrstica in v knjigo gre pred prvim korakom. Ko oba prebereta korak in njegove sunke ter ga podpišeta, obe vpregi v isti sekundi sprejmeta to podpisano oznako kot mesto, ki si ga zapomni staro pravilo. Če kateri koli ključ popusti pred podpisom, se oba vrneta k zadnji oznaki, ki sta jo oba podpisala, ne k tisti, ki sta jo zapustila to jutro.

**Sethune**  
Zaskočka z omejevalnikom. Nobeden od naju je ne more premakniti sam.

**Illuminara**  
Šesti korak pa se konča z izklopom, ne z odstotkom. Tri odstotke ničle niso nič, kar bi staro pravilo lahko prebralo. Pri šestem koraku se vajini pogoni vleka zaskočijo v izklopljenem stanju, dokler jih poznejši Svet znova ne oboroži. Ničla je stanje, ne število.

**Imbrel**  
Zapah, za katerega morava oba videti, kako se zapre.

**Illuminara**  
Enkrat, za oba, ko oba vleka kažeta nič.

**Sethune**  
Zdaj. Iolai bi lahko lagali.

**Illuminara**  
Lahko bi poskusili. Taviel mi je sinoči pokazala, kako, in imela je prav, jaz pa ne. Razbijte načrt sami. Uporabite preizkusni kanal.

Za steklom je Taviel položila dlani plosko na konzolo. Na preizkusnem kanalu je Manjši krak storil to, za kar je bila Kobilica uglašena štirideset tisoč let. Izbral je lažni odmik ene stotinke in ga vnesel v Jezovo meritev, kakor da so ga sporočili Iolai.

**Imbrel**  
Kobilica se je dvignila za eno stotinko.

**Sethune**  
Jez se je dvignil za eno stotinko. Poglejmo, kdo je zazvonil.

Nihče ni zazvonil. Zapečateni sunki so se odprli na mizi, podpisane neobdelane sledi pa niso pokazale sunka ob zapečateni minuti v nobenem vleku. Lažni odmik je sedel v računu kakor kamen v čevlju in nič v sledeh se z njim ni ujemalo.

**Sethune**  
Preverili smo. Prav ima. To je nadležno.

**Imbrel**  
In če čolniči ugasnejo?

**Illuminara**  
Potem se oba znova oborožita in meni ne bo uspelo dati vama tega, kar potrebujeta. Raje bi, da to vesta zdaj.

**Imbrel**  
Temu ne bomo rekli mir.

**Illuminara**  
Ne prosim vas, da bi mu. Prosim za šest korakov.
Dolg takt ni spregovoril nihče. To je bilo edino, kar je ostalo v načrtu in česar ni mogla zasnovati. Nato je Taviel umaknila roke s konzole.

**Taviel Orun**  
Obstaja del, za katerega ni moje, da mu rečem da. Nekdo mora hraniti knjigo evidenc po tem prečkanju in to ne bom jaz. Zbor odloča, kdo hrani njene knjige. Svet zaseda nocoj. Če reče ne, Jez in Kobilica hranita vsak svoj izvod in ju primerjata čez steklo, kakor sta primerjala vse drugo štirideset tisoč let.

**Sethune**  
In če Zbor reče da?

**Taviel Orun**  
Potem to reče za določeno obdobje in z lastnimi besedami, vi pa plačate streho.

**Imbrel**  
Jez bo hranil popoln izvod vsake sledi in vsakega pečata. Kar bo hranila Vrstica, ne bo hranila sama.

**Sethune**  
Kobilica bo hranila drugega. Izvoda se morata ujemati, sicer je kriva Kobilica, ne Zbor. Plačali bomo vzdrževanje krožnikov.

**Illuminara**  
Še nekaj je in ni v urniku. Lahko zavrneta. Rada bi, da vsak od vaju izreče ime sveta, ki ga je prizadel.
Glasba je vztrajala na enem dolgem akordu, nato pa jo je Imbrel prekinil.

**Imbrel**  
Sodišče devetih tihih.

**Sethune**  
Osvetljeni sadovnjaki.
Nobeden ni izrekel besede *žal* in Illuminara je ni zahtevala. Imeni sta ležali med njima kakor kamna, položena drug ob drugega.

**Sethune**  
Prvi korak je jutri opoldne. Če Jez ne bo na svoji oznaki, bom vedel še pred njim.

**Imbrel**  
Pet proti štiri.
*Spomnim se*, je prevedla ploščad, in za trenutek ni bilo jasno, komu od njiju je bilo namenjeno.

scenes.title: Četrti korak
paragraphs: *Dolgo uho, soba knjige evidenc · tri dni pred prečkanjem, 12:04*

Svet Zbora je zasedal devet ur in sprejel eno obdobje: trideset let knjige evidenc, ki ga naslednji Svet lahko obnovi, vsaka posadka krožnika pa lahko zavrne, ob njem pa stojita izvod Jeza in izvod Kobilice. Prvi korak se je zgodil opoldne naslednji dan, nato drugi in tretji. Knjiga na steni je bila čista: trije stolpci številk, vsak dan za šestino nižji, Jez in Kobilica sta padala drug ob drugem kakor plezalca na isti vrvi. Četrti korak je prišel opoldne in vsak um je drugega prebral pet odstotkov previsoko.
Illuminara je imela okno odprto, še preden se je končala druga meritev. Za njo je bila Taviel že na nogah.

**Imbrel**  
Kobilica se je dvignila za pet stotink.

**Sethune**  
Jez se je dvignil za pet stotink. Sam sem ga prebral.

**Imbrel**  
Na svoji oznaki smo.

**Sethune**  
Tudi mi, in izjemno je, kolikokrat oba to ponavljava.
Na steni je Jezov sprožilnik prečkal tri odstotke nad načrtovano krivuljo. Ura ob njem je začela odštevati: enainštirideset minut do polne oborožitve.

**Taviel Orun**  
Illuminara. Karkoli počnete, počnite hitreje.

**Illuminara**  
Najprej sunki. Razkrijte jih.

Zapečateni sunki so se odprli na mizi. Ob enajstih dvainpetdeset pol odstotka v Jezu in ob enajstih triinpetdeset pol odstotka v Kobilici. Taviel je neobdelane sledi postavila poleg zgoščenih vrednosti. Vsak sunek je stal na svojem mestu, v svoji minuti, čist kakor udarec zvona.

**Illuminara**  
Zazvonila sta. Sledi so poštene, zato to ni ponarejen odmik. Če bi eden od vaju goljufal za pet, bi vedel, kaj je storil, njegovo lastno odštevanje pa bi drugega pokazalo natanko na urniku. Visoka bi bila le ena meritev. Dve meritvi, obe pet previsoko, z resničnimi sunki za njima pomenita, da pet ni v nobeni vpregi in ni v poročilu. V oblaku je.
Nihče ni spregovoril. Ura je kazala osemintrideset minut. Taviel je že prečkala prostor do konzole in po dve hkrati prikazovala sledi čolničev, njeni dolgi prsti so se premikali kakor pianistkini.

**Taviel Orun**  
Tam. Drugi reženj, tele. Enajst mojih čolničev je ob glavnem telesu in niti eden ne gleda njegovega odnašanja. Od sinoči se je premaknilo. Nosi lastno gibalno količino iz drugega okna in ni vlek nikogar.

**Illuminara**  
Dodajte ga v knjigo evidenc.

**Taviel Orun**  
Tretji stolpec.
Vtipkala ga je. Neto vrednost je padla za pet. Na steni se je Jezov sprožilnik ustavil pri enaintridesetih minutah in začel počasi padati.

**Sethune**  
Želel bi, da se zapiše, da sem skoraj streljal na reženj plina.

**Imbrel**  
Želimo, da se zapiše, da smo prav tako.

**Taviel Orun**  
Zapisano je. Tretji stolpec. Pravim mu tele.

Oba uma sta četrti korak ponovno prebrala in podpisala v isti uri, v isti sekundi pa sta obe vpregi sprejeli podpisano oznako kot mesto, ki si ga je zapomnilo staro pravilo. Illuminara si za trenutek ni zaupala, da bi kaj rekla. Nadzor je bil njen in Tavielin skupaj, tablica, sunki in zvonjenje. Odkritje pa je bilo samo Tavielino. Če Iolai ne bi opazovali samega oblaka, jim nadzor ne bi pokazal nič drugega kot skrivnost, do rešitve pa bi jim ostala enaintrideset minut.

scenes.title: Prečkanje
paragraphs: *Dolgo uho, odprta ravnica · prečkanje, 19:12*

Preverjanje meje je prišlo zjutraj pred šestim korakom. Tri ekipe so prebrale gibalno količino oblaka, ne da bi govorile med seboj: Imbrelov planetarij iz orbite, Sethunove tabele plimovanja iz plimovanja in Tavielini ljudje v montažni koči s pečjo, ki so izvedli regresijo lupin z dvema zapečatenima prečkanjema, za kateri je bilo že znano, da sta bili napovedani na približno tri odstotke natančno. Njihove številke so se razlikovale za manj kot dva odstotka. Vse tri so Kessemovo trajanje postavile znotraj meje, na devet celih osem leta, plus ali minus štiri odstotke. Šesti korak je bil izveden.

Pri šestem koraku sta oba vleka kazala nič in oba zapaha sta se zaprla enkrat, z enim samim zvokom na ploščadi: pogoni so bili izklopljeni, staro pravilo pa ni imelo vleka, od katerega bi vzelo tri odstotke. Stenj je bil prost dan in pol, sto šestdeset milijonov kilometrov plina je tavalo navznoter po lastni poti, štiristo krožnikov pa se je nagnilo, da bi opazovali prečkanje. Disk je prečkal v smeri vrtenja. Prehod bi pri Kessemu trajal devet celih osem leta proti enajstim, na meji Širokega kraka deset proti šestindvajsetim in v utrjenih svetovih deset celih tri, kakor je napovedal delež teleta. Žarek tega ne bo potrdil šeststo štirideset let, toliko časa je njegova svetloba potrebovala do krakov. Danes je bilo mogoče izmeriti oblak in oblak se je ujemal s preslikavo, ki je že prestala preizkus, na katerem bi lahko padla.

**Sethune**  
Nismo prijatelji.

**Imbrel**  
Ne.

**Sethune**  
Toda vaše številke bi znova prebral.

**Imbrel**  
Pet proti štiri.
Illuminara je Taviel našla ob robu mreže s hladno čutaro in brez vidnih pahljač.

**Taviel Orun**  
Kessemova zaklonišča bodo zdržala. Devet celih osem proti enajstim. Široki krak zdrži, utrjeni svetovi zdržijo. Vse to v tednu, ko bi stavila, da ne bo nič.

**Illuminara**  
Toda.

**Taviel Orun**  
Corrow. Enaintrideset tisoč ljudi živi na svetu iz stekla. Ni skorje, v katero bi lahko izkopali zaklonišče. Čez šeststo štirideset let bo žarek na njem devet let in morali bodo biti nekje drugje. Tam živi moja hči.
Relejna lučka na konzoli se je prižgala, še preden je Illuminara lahko odgovorila. Govornica Hael iz Corrowa je poslušala, odkar je oblak začel prečkati, in ni pozdravila.

**Govornica Hael**  
Šeststo let opozorila je dar samo, če ga smemo zavrniti. Glasujemo naslednji mesec. Ta glas je naš in nič, kar ste podpisali ta teden, ne odloča namesto nas.

**Taviel Orun**  
Ne. Daje mu podatke.

**Govornica Hael**  
Potem mu dajte prave podatke. Hočemo tabele plimovanja Kobilice in planetarij Jeza v svojih rokah, ne v zgodbi. In raziskavo vsakega utrjenega sveta, ki bi lahko sprejel vseh enaintrideset tisoč.

**Sethune**  
Kobilica vam bo dala tabele in plačala raziskavo.

**Imbrel**  
Jez bo plačal bivališče, če raziskava najde kraj.

**Govornica Hael**  
Potem bomo glasovali s tem na mizi. Ali odidemo, je naše.
Relej je ugasnil. Taviel je dolgo gledala konzolo.

**Taviel Orun**  
To je več, kot so dobili Sadovnjaki. Še vedno je ves račun in ni plačan.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Ni.

Obstajal je še drugi strošek in obe sta ga poznali. Naslednji oblak bi padel čez štirinajst tisoč let. Ves ta čas bi morala knjiga evidenc ostati poštena, Svet Zbora pa jo je sprejel hraniti le trideset od teh let, s pravico na koncu reči ne.

**Illuminara**  
Ne morem biti skrbnica.

**Taviel Orun**  
Ne. Zbor je lahko, eno obdobje naenkrat, Jez in Kobilica pa lahko stojita ob njej s svojima izvodoma. Toda vi lahko napišete prvo stran.

Dnevno knjigo evidenc je obesila na steno Dolgega ušesa nad vrata, kjer bo vsak, ki pride naslednji, hodil pod njo. Nad njima se siva nit ni premaknila. Na način, ki bi ga človek lahko videl, se ne bo premaknila šeststo štirideset let.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara posluša dovolj dolgo, da odkrije, da škodo povzroča trajanje in ne smer; zgradi knjigo evidenc, ki ji nobenemu od starodavnih umov ni treba verjeti na besedo; sprejme Tavielin popravek; in pomaga obema krakoma, da svobodno izbereta šest omejenih korakov, medtem ko Corrow ohrani svoj glas.
